beats.words: I got early access to Claude Duet. And the first thing that struck me is a really weird thing to say about an app. It knows what it knows about me.
beats.point: The hook: he has Duet already, and the strange thing is how much it knew him on day one

picture.what: To camera, room treated (darkened and softened behind him)

beats.motion: still; the label types in on "early access"

beats.words: So what does it actually change if you already use Claude at work? Let me break it down.
beats.point: The question this piece answers, for people who already use Claude for work

picture.what: To camera, room treated (darkened and softened behind him)

beats.words: Duet is Anthropic's new Claude app, and it messages you first.
beats.point: It is the app that speaks first: the first message came from Duet, not from him

picture.what: Duet's first message on the phone, set in a phone frame on the ink desk: the welcome bubble, with ink redaction bars (cut paper on the ink desk, part of the look) over the name in 'Hi ...' and the 'K' avatar top right (the screen recording is silent; it plays under his voice, sped to fit the beat)
picture.source_label: CLAUDE DUET · ITS OWN SCREEN, 29 OCT

beats.motion: the bubble slides up as it arrives; slow push in

beats.words: Every few hours it checks your email, your calendar, Slack and whatever else you've connected.
beats.point: It checks the apps you already connected, on a timer

picture.what: Gmail, Google Calendar and Slack logos at equal size slide onto the queue rail, then a small mint counter ticks to "6,000+"

beats.motion: each logo slides in on its name; the counter on "whatever else"

beats.words: Each morning it sends you a short brief. And in the meantime, it drafts replies, meeting prep and documents for you.
beats.point: The morning brief and the drafts are real objects it makes and refreshes

picture.what: The Morning brief card Duet built, 'Morning brief for Friday 30 October', with ink redaction bars (cut paper on the ink desk, part of the look) over every line of the brief body (it names his ventures and people); only the title and the 'Refresh it at 6:30 every morning' line stay readable (the screen recording is silent; it plays under his voice, sped to fit the beat)
picture.source_label: CLAUDE DUET · ITS OWN SCREEN, 29 OCT

beats.motion: the card builds from blank to full, sped up; push in on the title

beats.words: Then it stops. Before it sends a message, pays for something, signs or deletes anything, it shows you what it's about to do. And it waits for your yes.
beats.point: It prepares, then stops: four kinds of action wait for a yes

picture.what: The approval queue (motion system): four drafted actions arrive in the queue, SEND A MESSAGE, PAY, SIGN, DELETE, each stopping at a lilac line with an empty YES pill beside it

beats.on_screen_text: OFF-LIMITS EVEN WITH A YES: TRADES, MOVING MONEY
beats.motion: each action slides in on its verb and halts at the line; the YES pills wait, unlit

beats.words: The setup is really seamless. Most apps ask you ten questions to customise your experience. Duet skips all that.
beats.point: No quiz: two screens and it is in

picture.what: The setup screens: 'Connect your apps' (Google Drive suite already connecting) then 'Get notified'; nothing private on these two screens (the screen recording is silent; it plays under his voice, sped to fit the beat)

beats.words: Anthropic says it carries over your memory, your skills and your connected apps from your Claude account.
beats.point: Anthropic says your Claude comes with it

picture.what: The Help Center line highlighted: 'Claude Duet carries over your memory, skills, and connected apps from your Claude account'
picture.source_label: CLAUDE HELP CENTER

beats.motion: slow push into the highlighted line

beats.words: I've lived my life in this Claude account for a while, and I've got everything connected. So it pretty much walked in already knowing me.
beats.point: Why it already knew him: he lives in his Claude account

picture.what: To camera, room treated (darkened and softened behind him)

beats.words: There is one catch. It's tied to one email account.
beats.point: The catch: one email account

picture.what: To camera, room treated (darkened and softened behind him)

beats.words: If you're anyone over the age of 15, you've probably got a few email accounts. And they're all a bit of a jumble. The one I connected is full of bills and not really my work stuff.
beats.point: Most people split their life across several inboxes, so one account sees only part of it

picture.what: To camera, room treated (darkened and softened behind him)

beats.words: And if your work email runs on Microsoft, Duet can't connect to it yet.
beats.point: Work email on Microsoft is out for now

picture.source_label: CLAUDE HELP CENTER

beats.words: So what did it do? It pulled a bunch of tasks for me.
beats.point: What it did first: it filled a task list on its own

picture.what: Tasks: the 'Active' and 'Up next' tabs, with ink redaction bars (cut paper on the ink desk, part of the look) over the item text (the screen recording is silent; it plays under his voice, sped to fit the beat)

do_not: No public word or pixel names him: his name in Duet's greeting, the 'K' avatar, the owner line on the Calendar scheduler and anything else that names him sits under an ink bar (floor 1)

Nothing private from his screen: the first task's two words (he says 'a job search' aloud; the screen never shows it), the inbox summary, his ventures (Mindmake, Legibility, Heartside, Full Time), the people, places, providers and amounts in the to-dos, the Google Play spend line, the morning brief's body and the Artifacts titles all sit under ink bars. A moment that cannot be covered cleanly is not used
Never a blur that leaves letters guessable; ink bars only
No reviewer or Reddit username on screen; Claire Vo and Lenny's Newsletter appear only because he names them
No on-screen label repeats what he says (the burned captions carry his words); a label adds a source, date, number or name
No figure or icon acting out an idea; every picture is his real screen, a checked page, a real logo or the queue
No named scheduling or note-taking company on screen: he names the categories, not companies
Never invent a word, number, label or picture; a gap goes back to Claude
acceptance: Watched end to end at full size, at the speed the audience sees it, by a reviewer who did not make the cut
Every spoken word heard continuously: no chopped syllable at any join (audio compared around each edit boundary)
Every picture lands on the words it proves, framing centred, logos at equal size, no shake left in
Brand matches the reference frame: wordmark, captions, palette and the intro sting
Fact, transport and editorial status reported separately; ready only when all three pass

take_edits.ruling: Krish, 2026-10-26: "Happy to cut those four slips as long as it doesn't make the output sound weird or glitchy.  That's just how I talk. Unless you think there are serious flaws in it, they're not really slips as much as they are just me talking naturally."
take_edits.rule: Keep everything he said as he said it. Cut only a serious flaw, only where the cut is inaudible (in the silence between words, under a picture), judged by ear at full volume. If it cannot be cut cleanly, keep it.
take_edits.none_proposed: No serious flaw in either take: no wrong fact, no legal risk. What he added (about 32% of the 5-minute and 29% of the 90-second is his own words) is how he talks and stays, including his asides "Anthropic have typically always been pretty good at waiting until you're approved", "I was very lucky to get on that early waitlist" and "Remember, no sending, no spending without your permission."

production_notes: 2026-10-31, Claude Code: both takes are on camera, 1080x1920 portrait, read against the current Teleprompter words (both hashes match the record). The screen recording (Claude duet run-through.mp4, 720x1560, 22 min 26 s, silent) and the shorter 'claude duet - video run through.mp4' (3 min 26 s, silent) are the proof; only the longer one is used. Timestamps in each beat are recording time.

The to-do list, the morning brief and the inbox summary are mostly private. Each is shown for its shape (a list arrived, a brief exists, it thought for minutes), with the private words under ink bars. If after covering, a beat reads as mostly bars, production stops and says which beat; Claude replaces it with a queue card from the checked facts.

Logos: Gmail, Google Calendar, Slack, Microsoft 365 and Claude fetched by their official brand pages at production, equal size, never redrawn. The Claude mark already in the repository is docs/plans/2026-10-09-friday/logos/claude-cream.svg.
The 36 HOURS beat uses the Reddit user's own figure ('I caught up in 36 hours'); the article already says 'a day and a half'.
